newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Commercial Bank sees net profit rising.
newsitem.headline: Commercial Bank sees net profit rising.

text.p: Commercial Bank of Korea expects its net profit to rise to 135 billion won in calendar 1996 from 92 billion won profit in 1995, a bank official said on Friday.
Cho Young-heung, manager of the bank's international department, also said at a UBS Securities Investor Forum that the bank's net profit was seen further expanding to around 203 billion won in 1997.
He said the bank's net income before provisions and tax was expected to rise by 12 to 14 percent a year for the next several years.
In 1996, it was seen at 480 billion won against 477 billion won last year, rising further to 540 billion won in 1997 and 617 billion in 1998.
Cho said the rises were linked to a redution in non-performing loans and loan loss provisions, and rising fee-based income. He did not give detailed figures.
"For the past two years, our loan policy has been so conservative our customers were complaining about shortages of loans," Cho said. "We expect to see loans rising by 15 to 16 percent this year."
